---
title: "ChIP signal sanity checks (§4.13b)"
output: html_document
---

```{r, setup}
# §4.13b — sanity checks on the raw bigWigAverageOverBed output, run after
# the aggregate_chip SLURM array (04-2-aggregate-ChIP.sh) + chip_agg.done.
#
# Memory design: at full scale there are 2430 ChIP files x ~424k windows.
# Materializing all of it as one long table (what 05's `load-data` chunk
# used to do before it was fixed) costs tens of GB for data that only needs
# to produce ~2430 per-sample scalars plus a ~424k x 6-mark averaged
# matrix. This script never holds more than one file's columns (~3 MB) or
# one mark's running window-accumulator (~3.4 MB) in memory at a time.
set.seed(getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_SEED", 42L))

dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
sanity_csv <- "qc/sanity_summary.csv"
append_sanity <- function(check_name, status, value, threshold, notes = "") {
  fwrite(
    data.table(
      check_name = check_name,
      status = status,
      value = value,
      threshold = threshold,
      notes = notes
    ),
    sanity_csv,
    append = TRUE
  )
}

aggregateOver <- rtracklayer::import("processed_data/aggregateOver.bed")
# chromhmm windows are excluded from every downstream ChIP table (05, and
# the aggregation script itself never dropped them at source) — restrict
# to the same window set everything else operates on, so the row-count
# check below (check 1) has the right expected value.
is_chip_window <- !startsWith(aggregateOver$name, "chromhmm")
window_names <- aggregateOver$name[is_chip_window]
window_width <- width(aggregateOver)[is_chip_window]
names(window_width) <- window_names
n_windows <- length(window_names)

file_metadata <- fread("processed_data/file_table.csv.gz")
file_metadata[,
  local_file := file.path(sample_dt_dir, paste0(basename(file_path), ".tab.gz"))
]
chip_files <- file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq"]
stopifnot(all(file.exists(chip_files$local_file)))
marks <- sort(unique(chip_files$experiment_type))
```


```{r, per-file-summary}
# Phase 1: one pass over all 2430 files, each producing a single small
# summary row. bigWigAverageOverBed's 8 columns are name size covered sum
# mean0 mean min max; `size` is skipped here (window width is already
# known from aggregateOver and is constant per window across all files, so
# re-reading it 2430 times would be pure duplication).
per_file_summary <- rbindlist(pbmcapply::pbmcmapply(
  FUN = function(file, this_ihec, this_mark, this_is_imputed) {
    dt <- fread(
      file,
      select = c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8),
      col.names = c("name", "covered", "sum", "mean0", "mean", "min", "max")
    )
    dt <- dt[!startsWith(name, "chromhmm")]

    widths_here <- window_width[dt$name]

    data.table(
      local_file = file,
      ihec = this_ihec,
      mark = this_mark,
      is_imputed = this_is_imputed,
      n_rows = nrow(dt),
      # check 1: structural integrity — truncated/corrupted bigwig output
      n_rows_ok = nrow(dt) == n_windows,
      # check 2: mean0 = sum/size, mean = sum/covered, covered <= size,
      # signal >= 0 => mean0 <= mean must always hold; a violation means
      # either corrupted arithmetic or an unexpectedly negative-valued track
      mean0_violations = sum(dt$mean0 > dt$mean + 1e-6, na.rm = TRUE),
      # check 3: signal tracks (p-value / enrichment) are non-negative by
      # construction; a negative min means the wrong bigwig type got
      # aggregated here
      min_violations = sum(dt$min < -1e-6, na.rm = TRUE),
      # check 4: fraction of this sample's windows where less than half the
      # window width is actually covered by the bigwig — mean/mean0 are
      # unreliable extrapolations from very sparse coverage
      coverage_low_frac = mean(dt$covered / widths_here < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_score = median(dt$mean, na.rm = TRUE),
      zero_frac = mean(dt$mean == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      # check 8 (per-file simplification): 99.9th percentile of this
      # sample's per-window max — used below to flag samples with extreme
      # localized spikes (blacklist regions / PCR-duplication hotspots)
      max_p999 = quantile(dt$max, 0.999, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  },
  file = chip_files$local_file,
  this_ihec = chip_files$epirr_id_without_version,
  this_mark = chip_files$experiment_type,
  this_is_imputed = chip_files$uuid == "imputed",
  SIMPLIFY = FALSE
))

fwrite(per_file_summary, "qc/chip_per_file_summary.csv.gz")
```


```{r, structural-checks}
# checks 1-3: hard structural/arithmetic invariants. WARN (not stopifnot) —
# this is a sanity notebook, not a pipeline gate; a violation here should be
# investigated, not silently crash 04/05.
n_bad_rowcount <- per_file_summary[, sum(!n_rows_ok)]
append_sanity(
  "chip_row_count_integrity",
  ifelse(n_bad_rowcount == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  n_bad_rowcount, 0,
  sprintf("%d/%d files have row count != %d", n_bad_rowcount, nrow(per_file_summary), n_windows)
)

total_mean0_violations <- per_file_summary[, sum(mean0_violations)]
append_sanity(
  "chip_mean0_le_mean_invariant",
  ifelse(total_mean0_violations == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  total_mean0_violations, 0,
  "count of windows across all files where mean0 > mean (should never happen for non-negative signal)"
)

total_min_violations <- per_file_summary[, sum(min_violations)]
append_sanity(
  "chip_nonnegative_signal",
  ifelse(total_min_violations == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  total_min_violations, 0,
  "count of windows across all files where min < 0"
)
```


```{r, per-sample-outlier-checks}
# check 5: per-sample median signal, robust z-score within mark. MAD-based
# (not SD-based) to match the project's existing convention for skewed
# per-sample metrics (see 03's variability dip-test chunk) and to avoid a
# single extreme outlier sample inflating the SD used to judge itself.
per_file_summary[, median_z := {
  med <- median(median_score)
  mad_val <- mad(median_score)
  if (mad_val == 0) rep(0, .N) else (median_score - med) / mad_val
}, by = mark]
outlier_samples <- per_file_summary[abs(median_z) > 3]
append_sanity(
  "chip_per_sample_signal_outlier",
  ifelse(nrow(outlier_samples) == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  nrow(outlier_samples), 3,
  sprintf("samples with |median signal z-score| > 3: %s", paste(outlier_samples$local_file, collapse = "; "))
)

# check 6: per-sample zero-inflation — flags samples with abnormally flat/
# zero signal (potential failed ChIP). NOT MAD-z: zero_frac has a large
# point-mass at (or near) 0 for most marks (median zero_frac == 0 for
# H3K27ac/H3K36me3/H3K4me3/H3K9me3 in practice), which collapses the MAD to
# a tiny nonzero value and makes MAD-z explode for any sample even slightly
# above that near-zero floor — empirically this flagged ~27% of samples,
# an implausible failure rate. One-sided upper Tukey fence (Q3 + 3*IQR)
# is the standard robust alternative for a skewed, floor-heavy metric where
# only the upper tail is a real concern (unusually low zero_frac is not a
# problem in the way unusually high zero_frac is).
per_file_summary[, zero_frac_upper_fence := {
  q1 <- quantile(zero_frac, 0.25)
  q3 <- quantile(zero_frac, 0.75)
  rep(q3 + 3 * (q3 - q1), .N)
}, by = mark]
zero_outliers <- per_file_summary[zero_frac > zero_frac_upper_fence]
append_sanity(
  "chip_zero_inflation_outlier",
  ifelse(nrow(zero_outliers) == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  nrow(zero_outliers), 3,
  sprintf("samples with zero-fraction above per-mark Q3+3*IQR: %s", paste(zero_outliers$local_file, collapse = "; "))
)

# check 8: per-sample extreme max-signal spikes. Same rationale as check 6
# — max_p999 is heavily right-skewed (up to ~17x the median for H3K4me3),
# and only unusually HIGH values indicate a real spike artifact (blacklist
# region / PCR-duplication hotspot); a one-sided upper Tukey fence avoids
# both the zero-inflation MAD collapse risk and flagging low values that
# aren't actually a problem.
per_file_summary[, max_p999_upper_fence := {
  q1 <- quantile(max_p999, 0.25)
  q3 <- quantile(max_p999, 0.75)
  rep(q3 + 3 * (q3 - q1), .N)
}, by = mark]
spike_outliers <- per_file_summary[max_p999 > max_p999_upper_fence]
append_sanity(
  "chip_extreme_spike_outlier",
  ifelse(nrow(spike_outliers) == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  nrow(spike_outliers), 3,
  sprintf("samples with max_p999 above per-mark Q3+3*IQR: %s", paste(spike_outliers$local_file, collapse = "; "))
)

# check 4 (file-level rollup): fraction of files where >10% of windows are
# under-covered — a systemic coverage problem rather than a one-off window
frac_files_low_coverage <- per_file_summary[, mean(coverage_low_frac > 0.10)]
append_sanity(
  "chip_coverage_completeness",
  ifelse(frac_files_low_coverage <= 0.05, "PASS", "WARN"),
  frac_files_low_coverage, 0.05,
  "fraction of files where >10% of windows have covered/size < 0.5"
)
```


```{r, observed-vs-imputed-check}
# check 7: imputed ChIP tracks (uuid == "imputed") are model outputs and may
# sit on a different dynamic range than observed tracks; silently mixing
# them (as 05 does — both feed the same `score`/gene_expression pipeline)
# would bias marks unevenly across samples if the scales don't match.
obs_imp_summary <- per_file_summary[, .(
  median_observed = median(median_score[!is_imputed]),
  median_imputed   = median(median_score[is_imputed])
), by = mark]
obs_imp_summary[, ratio := median_imputed / median_observed]
bad_marks <- obs_imp_summary[ratio < 0.5 | ratio > 2, mark]
append_sanity(
  "chip_observed_vs_imputed_scale",
  ifelse(length(bad_marks) == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  length(bad_marks), 0,
  sprintf("marks with imputed/observed median ratio outside [0.5, 2]: %s", paste(bad_marks, collapse = ", "))
)
```


```{r, window-level-accumulation}
# Phase 2: per-mark, cohort-averaged signal at every window. Computed with
# a sequential running sum per mark (not one big collected matrix) so peak
# memory stays at one window-length vector (~3.4 MB) per mark in flight;
# the 6 marks are done in parallel, so peak memory is ~6 vectors (~20 MB),
# not 2430.
window_mean_by_mark <- pbmcapply::pbmcmapply(
  FUN = function(mark) {
    mark_files <- chip_files[experiment_type == mark, local_file]
    acc <- numeric(n_windows)
    n_ok <- 0L
    for (f in mark_files) {
      dt <- fread(f, select = c(1, 6), col.names = c("name", "mean"))
      dt <- dt[!startsWith(name, "chromhmm")]
      idx <- match(window_names, dt$name)
      if (anyNA(idx)) next # row mismatch already flagged by check 1
      acc <- acc + dt$mean[idx]
      n_ok <- n_ok + 1L
    }
    acc / n_ok
  },
  mark = marks,
  SIMPLIFY = TRUE
)
rownames(window_mean_by_mark) <- window_names
colnames(window_mean_by_mark) <- marks

window_position <- sub("_[0-9]+$", "", window_names)

# Window -> (Event Type, transcript_filter) stratum, via the ID embedded in
# each window name (format "<position>_<ID>", same tstrsplit convention 05
# uses). A given genomic event gets a distinct integer ID per
# transcript_filter (event_annotations_dt has one row per (event_id,
# transcript_filter) pair — confirmed empirically: every event_id appears
# exactly 3 times, once per filter, each with its own ID), so this join is
# exact, not an approximation.
window_id <- as.integer(tstrsplit(window_names, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[2]])
event_annotations_dt <- fread(
  "processed_data/event_annotations_dt.csv.gz",
  select = c("ID", "Event Type", "transcript_filter")
)
window_strata <- event_annotations_dt[
  data.table(ID = window_id),
  on = "ID",
  .(`Event Type`, transcript_filter)
]
```


```{r, viz-distributions}
# viz 1: density of raw + log1p signal per mark x window-position-type.
# Expected: raw right-skewed; log1p approximately log-normal. Active marks
# (H3K4me3, H3K27ac) should show a bimodal log1p distribution (background
# lobe near 0 + signal lobe); broad marks (H3K27me3, H3K36me3, H3K9me3)
# should be unimodal with broader spread.
pdf("qc/distributions/chip_signal_distributions.pdf", width = 9, height = 5)
for (mark in marks) {
  for (pos in unique(window_position)) {
    vals <- window_mean_by_mark[window_position == pos, mark]
    if (length(vals) < 2 || all(vals == 0)) next
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    hist(vals,
      breaks = 50, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
      main = paste(mark, pos, "- raw"), xlab = "mean signal"
    )
    hist(log1p(vals),
      breaks = 50, col = "darkorange", border = "white",
      main = paste(mark, pos, "- log1p"), xlab = "log1p(mean signal)"
    )
    par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  }
}
dev.off()
```


```{r, viz-mark-correlation}
# viz 2: mark-mark correlation across windows (cohort-averaged signal),
# computed separately per (Event Type, transcript_filter) stratum rather
# than pooled across all windows. Pooling mixes SE (~150k windows) with RI
# (~9k windows) and three highly overlapping transcript_filters
# (transcripts is a superset of tsl_filtered, which is a superset of
# biotype_filtered — same underlying events, filtered annotation), which
# risks a Simpson's-paradox-style distortion: a pooled correlation can
# differ in sign from every individual stratum's correlation. Known
# finding (see project memory): co-occurrence is all-positive even for
# antagonistic pairs (e.g. H3K27ac vs H3K27me3) — a chromatin-fingerprint
# confound, not event-specific regulation. Each stratum is checked against
# this independently; a negative pair within a stratum is more informative
# than one from a pooled computation, since it isn't attributable to
# cross-stratum mixing.
strata <- unique(window_strata[!is.na(`Event Type`)])

pdf("qc/distributions/chip_mark_correlation.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)
mark_cor_all <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(strata))) {
  this_event_type <- strata$`Event Type`[i]
  this_filter <- strata$transcript_filter[i]
  in_stratum <- window_strata$`Event Type` == this_event_type &
    window_strata$transcript_filter == this_filter
  in_stratum[is.na(in_stratum)] <- FALSE
  if (sum(in_stratum) < 10) next # too few windows for a meaningful correlation

  mark_cor <- cor(window_mean_by_mark[in_stratum, , drop = FALSE], method = "spearman")
  stratum_key <- paste(this_event_type, this_filter, sep = "_")
  mark_cor_all[[stratum_key]] <- mark_cor

  image(
    mark_cor,
    col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50),
    breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 51),
    axes = FALSE,
    main = sprintf("Mark-mark signal correlation (Spearman)\n%s / %s (n=%d windows)",
      this_event_type, this_filter, sum(in_stratum))
  )
  axis(1, at = seq(0, 1, length.out = ncol(mark_cor)), labels = colnames(mark_cor), las = 2)
  axis(2, at = seq(0, 1, length.out = nrow(mark_cor)), labels = rownames(mark_cor), las = 2)

  n_negative_pairs <- sum(mark_cor[upper.tri(mark_cor)] < 0)
  append_sanity(
    paste0("chip_mark_correlation_all_positive_", stratum_key),
    ifelse(n_negative_pairs == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
    n_negative_pairs, 0,
    sprintf("%s/%s (n=%d windows): count of mark pairs with negative correlation (0 expected per known fingerprint-confound finding)",
      this_event_type, this_filter, sum(in_stratum))
  )
}
dev.off()

fwrite(
  rbindlist(lapply(names(mark_cor_all), function(k) {
    m <- mark_cor_all[[k]]
    dt <- as.data.table(m, keep.rownames = "mark_row")
    dt[, stratum := k]
  })),
  "qc/chip_mark_correlation.csv"
)
```


```{r, sample-axis-correlation-test}
# Test for the window-axis-vs-sample-axis hypothesis: the window-axis
# correlation above (does mark A's cohort-averaged level at location X
# correlate with mark B's level at X, across many X?) showed negative
# pairs for antagonistic marks in every stratum — the opposite of the
# project memory's "all-positive mark co-occurrence" finding. Hypothesis:
# that finding was computed on a different axis — for a FIXED location,
# do samples with elevated mark A also show elevated mark B, across
# samples (averaged over many locations)? This is the "fingerprint" axis:
# a global per-sample activity/accessibility level that could lift
# multiple marks together regardless of their spatial antagonism. If
# reproduced here but not on the window axis, the two findings are
# compatible, not contradictory.
#
# Feasibility: a full sample-axis correlation needs, for a set of windows,
# every sample's value at each window (not just the cohort average used
# above) — the thing that made the original `histone_dt` load 1e9 rows
# and ~82 GB. Restricting to a modest random subset of windows per
# stratum keeps this to a third full pass over the 2430 files, but with
# only ~3000 of ~424k rows kept per file (2 columns), not the full table.
n_windows_per_stratum <- 500
set.seed(getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_SEED", 42L))
sample_window_names <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(strata)), function(i) {
  this_event_type <- strata$`Event Type`[i]
  this_filter <- strata$transcript_filter[i]
  in_stratum <- which(
    window_strata$`Event Type` == this_event_type &
      window_strata$transcript_filter == this_filter
  )
  sample(window_names[in_stratum], min(n_windows_per_stratum, length(in_stratum)))
}))

sample_axis_long <- rbindlist(pbmcapply::pbmcmapply(
  FUN = function(file, this_ihec, this_mark) {
    dt <- fread(file, select = c(1, 6), col.names = c("name", "mean"))
    dt <- dt[name %in% sample_window_names]
    dt[, ihec := this_ihec]
    dt[, mark := this_mark]
    dt
  },
  file = chip_files$local_file,
  this_ihec = chip_files$epirr_id_without_version,
  this_mark = chip_files$experiment_type,
  SIMPLIFY = FALSE
))
sample_axis_wide <- dcast(sample_axis_long, ihec + name ~ mark, value.var = "mean", fun.aggregate = mean)

# Fisher z-transform average — the statistically correct way to average
# correlation coefficients (a naive arithmetic mean of r is biased,
# especially away from 0).
fisher_avg <- function(r_vec) {
  r_vec <- r_vec[is.finite(r_vec) & abs(r_vec) < 1]
  if (length(r_vec) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  tanh(mean(atanh(r_vec)))
}

name_to_stratum <- window_strata[match(sample_window_names, window_names)]
name_to_stratum[, name := sample_window_names]

sample_axis_cor_all <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(strata))) {
  this_event_type <- strata$`Event Type`[i]
  this_filter <- strata$transcript_filter[i]
  stratum_key <- paste(this_event_type, this_filter, sep = "_")
  stratum_names <- name_to_stratum[
    `Event Type` == this_event_type & transcript_filter == this_filter,
    name
  ]

  # for each sampled window: one 6x6 correlation matrix ACROSS SAMPLES
  # (~405 data points per window — plenty for a stable per-window estimate)
  per_window_cors <- lapply(stratum_names, function(nm) {
    sub <- sample_axis_wide[name == nm, ..marks]
    if (nrow(sub) < 30) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    tryCatch(
      cor(sub, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  })
  per_window_cors <- per_window_cors[!sapply(per_window_cors, is.null)]

  # average those per-window sample-axis matrices across all sampled
  # windows in this stratum, to get one representative "fingerprint" matrix
  avg_cor <- matrix(NA_real_,
    nrow = length(marks), ncol = length(marks),
    dimnames = list(marks, marks)
  )
  for (r1 in marks) {
    for (r2 in marks) {
      r_vals <- sapply(per_window_cors, function(m) m[r1, r2])
      avg_cor[r1, r2] <- fisher_avg(r_vals)
    }
  }
  sample_axis_cor_all[[stratum_key]] <- avg_cor
}

fwrite(
  rbindlist(lapply(names(sample_axis_cor_all), function(k) {
    m <- sample_axis_cor_all[[k]]
    dt <- as.data.table(m, keep.rownames = "mark_row")
    dt[, stratum := k]
  })),
  "qc/chip_sample_axis_correlation.csv"
)
```


```{r, axis-comparison}
# Direct comparison, per mark pair per stratum: window-axis r vs
# sample-axis r. This is the actual test of the hypothesis above — not
# just plausible reasoning, real numbers from the same data.
comparison_rows <- list()
mark_pairs <- combn(marks, 2)
for (stratum_key in names(mark_cor_all)) {
  window_m <- mark_cor_all[[stratum_key]]
  sample_m <- sample_axis_cor_all[[stratum_key]]
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(mark_pairs))) {
    m1 <- mark_pairs[1, j]
    m2 <- mark_pairs[2, j]
    comparison_rows[[length(comparison_rows) + 1]] <- data.table(
      stratum = stratum_key, mark1 = m1, mark2 = m2,
      window_axis_r = window_m[m1, m2],
      sample_axis_r = sample_m[m1, m2]
    )
  }
}
axis_comparison <- rbindlist(comparison_rows)
fwrite(axis_comparison, "qc/chip_axis_comparison.csv")

pdf("qc/distributions/chip_axis_comparison.pdf", width = 7, height = 6)
plot(
  axis_comparison$window_axis_r, axis_comparison$sample_axis_r,
  xlab = "window axis (spatial) correlation", ylab = "sample axis (fingerprint) correlation",
  pch = 16, xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1),
  main = "Window-axis vs sample-axis mark correlation"
)
abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey")
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 3, col = "blue")
text(
  axis_comparison$window_axis_r, axis_comparison$sample_axis_r,
  labels = paste(axis_comparison$mark1, axis_comparison$mark2, sep = "-"),
  cex = 0.6, pos = 3
)
dev.off()

n_sample_axis_negative <- axis_comparison[, sum(sample_axis_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)]
n_window_axis_negative <- axis_comparison[, sum(window_axis_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)]
append_sanity(
  "chip_sample_vs_window_axis_hypothesis",
  ifelse(n_sample_axis_negative < n_window_axis_negative, "PASS", "WARN"),
  n_sample_axis_negative, n_window_axis_negative,
  sprintf(
    "hypothesis: memory's all-positive finding is on the sample axis (per-window, across-sample correlation, 'fingerprint'), not the window axis (spatial, across-window correlation). sample_axis negative pairs=%d, window_axis negative pairs=%d (out of %d stratum x pair combinations). PASS if sample axis has fewer negative pairs than window axis.",
    n_sample_axis_negative, n_window_axis_negative, nrow(axis_comparison)
  )
)
```


```{r, viz-per-sample}
# viz 3: per-sample outlier scatter — median signal per sample, faceted by
# mark, outliers (|z|>3, checks 5/6/8) highlighted.
pdf("qc/distributions/chip_per_sample_outliers.pdf", width = 9, height = 6)
for (this_mark in marks) {
  sub_dt <- per_file_summary[mark == this_mark]
  is_outlier <- abs(sub_dt$median_z) > 3
  plot(
    seq_len(nrow(sub_dt)), sub_dt$median_score,
    col = ifelse(is_outlier, "red", "black"),
    pch = ifelse(is_outlier, 17, 16),
    main = paste("Per-sample median signal -", this_mark),
    xlab = "sample index", ylab = "median signal"
  )
  if (any(is_outlier)) {
    legend("topright", legend = "outlier (|z|>3)", pch = 17, col = "red", bty = "n")
  }
}
dev.off()

# viz 4: coverage completeness (per-file fraction of low-coverage windows)
pdf("qc/distributions/chip_coverage_completeness.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)
hist(
  per_file_summary$coverage_low_frac,
  breaks = 50, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
  main = "Per-file fraction of windows with covered/size < 0.5",
  xlab = "fraction of low-coverage windows"
)
dev.off()

# viz 5: zero-inflation per mark
pdf("qc/distributions/chip_zero_inflation.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)
boxplot(
  zero_frac ~ mark,
  data = per_file_summary,
  main = "Per-sample zero-signal fraction by mark",
  xlab = "mark", ylab = "fraction of windows with mean == 0", las = 2
)
dev.off()

# viz 6: observed vs imputed signal scale
pdf("qc/distributions/chip_observed_vs_imputed.pdf", width = 8, height = 5)
boxplot(
  median_score ~ interaction(mark, is_imputed, sep = " / "),
  data = per_file_summary,
  main = "Per-sample median signal: observed vs imputed",
  xlab = "mark / is_imputed", ylab = "median signal", las = 2
)
dev.off()
```
